Three of the four highest-grossing films, including *Avatar* at the top, were written and directed by [James Cameron](/wiki/James_Cameron "James Cameron").

With a worldwide box-office gross of over $2.9 billion, *Avatar* is proclaimed to be the "highest-grossing" film, but such claims usually refer to [theatrical](/wiki/Movie_theatre "Movie theatre") revenues only and do not take into account [home video](/wiki/Home_video "Home video") and [television](/wiki/Television "Television") income, which can form a significant portion of a film's earnings. Once revenue from home entertainment is factored in, it is not immediately clear which film is the most successful. *[Titanic](/wiki/Titanic_(1997_film) "Titanic (1997 film)")* earned $1.2 billion from [video](/wiki/Video "Video") and [DVD](/wiki/DVD-Video "DVD-Video") sales and rentals,[[1]](#cite_note-titanic-sales-1) in addition to the $2.2 billion it grossed in theaters. While complete sales data are not available for *Avatar*, it earned $345 million from the sale of sixteen million DVD and [Blu-ray](/wiki/Blu-ray "Blu-ray") units in North America,[[2]](#cite_note-2) and ultimately sold a total of thirty million DVD and Blu-ray units worldwide.[[3]](#cite_note-3) After home video income is accounted for, both films have earned over $3 billion each. Television [broadcast](/wiki/Broadcasting "Broadcasting") rights also substantially add to a film's earnings and, as of 2010, a film often earned the equivalent of as much as 20–25% of its theatrical box office for two television runs, on top of [pay-per-view](/wiki/Pay-per-view "Pay-per-view") revenues;[[4]](#cite_note-4) *Titanic* earned a further $55 million from the [NBC](/wiki/NBC "NBC") and [HBO](/wiki/HBO "HBO") broadcast rights,[[1]](#cite_note-titanic-sales-1) equating to about 9% of its North American gross.

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/01/El_Capitan_at_fall.jpg/250px-El_Capitan_at_fall.jpg)](/wiki/File:El_Capitan_at_fall.jpg)

Yosemite in [autumn](/wiki/Autumn "Autumn")

Yosemite has a [Mediterranean climate](/wiki/Mediterranean_climate "Mediterranean climate") ([Köppen climate classification](/wiki/K%C3%B6ppen_climate_classification "Köppen climate classification") *Csa*), meaning most precipitation falls during the mild winter, and the other seasons are nearly dry (less than three percent of precipitation falls during the long, hot summers). Because of [orographic lift](/wiki/Orographic_lift "Orographic lift"), precipitation increases with elevation up to 8,000 feet (2,400 m) where it slowly decreases to the crest. Precipitation amounts vary from 36 inches (910 mm) at 4,000 feet (1,200 m) elevation to 50 inches (1,300 mm) at 8,600 feet (2,600 m). Snow does not typically accumulate until November in the high country. It deepens into March or early April.[[104]](#cite_note-climate-104)

Mean daily temperatures range from 25 °F (−4 °C) to 53 °F (12 °C) at Tuolumne Meadows at 8,600 feet (2,600 m). At the Wawona Entrance (elevation 5,130 feet or 1,560 metres), mean daily temperature ranges from 36 to 67 °F (2 to 19 °C). At the lower elevations below 5,000 feet (1,500 m), temperatures are hotter; the mean daily high temperature at Yosemite Valley (elevation 3,966 feet or 1,209 metres) varies from 46 to 90 °F (8 to 32 °C). At elevations above 8,000 feet (2,400 m), the hot, dry summer temperatures are moderated by frequent summer thunderstorms, along with snow that can persist into July. The combination of dry vegetation, low relative humidity, and thunderstorms results in frequent lightning-caused [fires](/wiki/Wildfire "Wildfire") as well.[[104]](#cite_note-climate-104)

At park headquarters (elevation 4,018 ft or 1,225 m), January averages 38.0 °F (3.3 °C), while July averages 73.3 °F (22.9 °C). In summer, the nights are much cooler than the days. [Teide](/wiki/Teide "Teide"), still an [active volcano](/wiki/Active_volcano "Active volcano") in [Tenerife](/wiki/Tenerife "Tenerife"), Canary Islands, is the tallest peak in Spain.

Mainland Spain is a rather [mountainous](/wiki/Mountainous "Mountainous") landmass, dominated by high [plateaus](/wiki/Plateau "Plateau") and mountain chains. After the Pyrenees, the main mountain ranges are the [Cordillera Cantábrica](/wiki/Cantabrian_Mountains "Cantabrian Mountains") (Cantabrian Range), [Sistema Ibérico](/wiki/Sistema_Ib%C3%A9rico "Sistema Ibérico") (Iberian System), [Sistema Central](/wiki/Sistema_Central "Sistema Central") (Central System), [Montes de Toledo](/wiki/Montes_de_Toledo "Montes de Toledo"), [Sierra Morena](/wiki/Sierra_Morena "Sierra Morena") and the [Sistema Bético](/wiki/Sistema_B%C3%A9tico "Sistema Bético") (Baetic System) whose highest peak, the 3,478-metre-high (11,411-foot) [Mulhacén](/wiki/Mulhac%C3%A9n "Mulhacén"), located in [Sierra Nevada](/wiki/Sierra_Nevada_(Spain) "Sierra Nevada (Spain)"), is the highest elevation in the Iberian Peninsula. The highest point in Spain is the [Teide](/wiki/Teide "Teide"), a 3,718-metre (12,198 ft) active [volcano](/wiki/Volcano "Volcano") in the Canary Islands. The [Meseta Central](/wiki/Meseta_Central "Meseta Central") (often translated as 'Inner Plateau') is a vast plateau in the heart of peninsular Spain split in two by the Sistema Central.

There are several major [rivers in Spain](/wiki/Rivers_in_Spain "Rivers in Spain") such as the [Tagus](/wiki/Tagus "Tagus") (*Tajo*), [Ebro](/wiki/Ebro "Ebro"), [Guadiana](/wiki/Guadiana_River "Guadiana River"), [Douro](/wiki/Douro "Douro") (*Duero*), [Guadalquivir](/wiki/Guadalquivir "Guadalquivir"), [Júcar](/wiki/J%C3%BAcar_River "Júcar River"), [Segura](/wiki/Segura_(river) "Segura (river)"), [Turia](/wiki/Turia_River "Turia River") and [Minho](/wiki/Minho_River "Minho River") (*Miño*).
